result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): The two emails are almost the same: both are accurate, own the mistake plainly, give the refund dates, ask nothing of the owner, and handle overdraft fees correctly. B's banner is better. It says 'We charged you $29 twice' to the account owner, while A's banner shifts to the passive 'A billing error… charged some accounts', which reads oddly on an affected owner's own billing page. B also adds the useful note that the banner should only show on affected accounts. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both emails follow the fact sheet closely: each opens with the double $29 charge, names the billing job running twice as Shiftwell's fault, gives the 4 March and 11 March refund dates, says owners need do nothing, and handles overdraft fees as reply-and-review without promising reimbursement. A's banner is tighter and stays in the active voice ('We charged you $29 twice'), while B's banner says 'A billing error... charged some accounts' and so does not plainly say Shiftwell caused it. B also repeats the apology. B's note about not claiming the bug is fixed is thoughtful, but A is slightly cleaner overall.
